label: Both hosts expose exactly the same 60 repo skills with identical ids: opencode debug skill (v1 1.19.3) returns 73 rows of which 60 are under the repo root, and GET /api/skill (v2 2.0.32) returns 74 rows of which 60 are under the repo root; the id sets are identical and every nested mode packet (cli-opencode, sk-code-opencode, deep-research, mcp-figma, sk-create-skill, ...) is a separate skill on both. The count equals the filesystem census find .skilled/skills -name SKILL.md = 60, so the repo's parent-hub plus nested-packet layout requires no change for either version.

Both versions follow the symlinked skill roots and dedupe by resolved real path: .opencode/skills and .claude/skills are both symlinks to ../.skilled/skills (readlink returns ../.skilled/skills for each, pwd -P resolves to .skilled/skills), and two roots over 60 files yields 60 rows on both hosts rather than 120. The repo's duplicate-root exposure is therefore not an expose-twice risk on either version.

The two versions disagree on which symlinked root they report for five shared ids: v1 attributes cli-codex, cli-devin, sk-code-quality, sk-create-frontmatter and sk-create-with-human-voice to .claude/skills/... while v2 attributes all 60 to .opencode/skills/..., for the same underlying file. Any consumer keyed on the reported path string (path-prefix hook, location-keyed cache, string dedupe) will disagree across versions for those ids and must normalise with realpath.

The built-in skill layer differs by binary in both name and mechanism: v1-only customize-opencode (location '<built-in>'), v2-only opencode (path /builtin/opencode.md) plus the operator-global 'report' skill. A raw skill-count assertion (73 vs 74) can never be a compatibility check on its own.

Both versions catalogue three vendored dependency skills from .opencode/skills/sk-design/sk-design-md-generator/backend/node_modules/playwright-core/lib/tools/skills/ (playwright-cli, playwright-component-testing, playwright-trace). Behaviour is identical on both hosts so it is not a compatibility break, but it occupies 3 of the 60 slots and an npm install under that backend can change the exposed catalog on both versions at once, making a '60 skills' acceptance check fragile.

Frontmatter census over the 60 repo SKILL.md files: name 57/60, description 57/60, allowed-tools 57/60, version 57/60, metadata 11/60, argument-hint 4/60, disable-model-invocation 0/60, license 0/60. The three lacking name/description/allowed-tools/version are exactly the vendored playwright skills, which both hosts still list with directory-derived ids, so frontmatter name is optional on both versions and the directory basename is the fallback id. disable-model-invocation is used by no repo skill, so its cross-version semantics are untested by the repo.

.skilled/skills/sk-communication contains no SKILL.md at all, only cli-communication-projection/{dist,node_modules}, so it is invisible to both v1 and v2 (which key on a file literally named SKILL.md). It is a top-level directory under the skills root that the catalog silently drops on both versions: version-neutral, but a repo-side dead entry.

Skill permission gating is NOT settled: no "skill" permission key exists in opencode.json or .opencode/*.json, and opencode debug config produced no readable permission projection, so v2's skill action and its v1 counterpart remain unverified. What is established is the read surface: v1's list payload carries {name, description, location, content} and v2's carries {id, name, description, path, content}, so allowed-tools, version, argument-hint and metadata influence nothing observable through either catalog API.
On both versions the exposed skill set is exactly every SKILL.md found under a discovered root, deduped by resolved real path; the skill id is the basename of the directory containing that SKILL.md.
A skill directory without a file literally named SKILL.md is invisible on both v1 1.19.3 and v2 2.0.32.
